title: Be honest… not surface-level honest, not the kind you show people… the kind that sits with you in silence when no one is watching.
paragraphs: Be honest… not surface-level honest, not the kind you show people… the kind that sits with you in silence when no one is watching.
Are you following Jesus… or have you carefully constructed a version of Him that never confronts you?
Because that version exists. And it’s everywhere.

A Jesus who agrees with everything you already believe.
A Jesus who never calls out your sin—just your struggles.
A Jesus who comforts, but never corrects.
A Jesus who fits your lifestyle instead of transforming it.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
That Jesus isn’t real.
You didn’t reject Him outright—you reshaped Him quietly.

You kept the parts that feel good.
Ignored the parts that cut deep.
Reinterpreted the parts that demand surrender.
And somewhere along the way… you stopped following Him, and started leading Him.

You wouldn’t say it out loud.
But your life says it clearly.

You pray—but only when it’s convenient.
You listen—but only when it affirms you.
You obey—but only when it doesn’t cost you.
God saw it.

That moment you knew what was right… and chose what was easy.
That conviction you silenced because it interrupted your plans.
That compromise you justified because “everyone else is doing it.”
You knew.
And still… you called it “following Jesus.”
But Scripture doesn’t leave room for a customized Christ.

Jesus said in Luke 9:23,
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.”
Read that again.

Deny yourself.
Not express yourself.
Not protect yourself.
Deny.

Take up your cross.
Not your comfort.
Not your preferences.
Your cross.
Daily.

This isn’t a casual association.
This is surrender.
And here’s where it gets uncomfortable…
Because deep down, you already feel the tension.

You know when you’re bending truth to fit your life.
You know when you’re avoiding conviction.
You know when you’ve replaced obedience with explanation.
That quiet unease you keep pushing away?

That’s not guilt to be ignored.
That’s mercy trying to wake you up.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
There’s a difference between knowing about Jesus and actually following Him.

One requires agreement.
The other requires death.
Jesus didn’t come to improve your life while leaving you in control.
He came to save you—from sin, from self, from the illusion that you can be your own authority.

Romans 6:23 says,
“For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.”

Not behavior modification.
Not spiritual comfort.
Death… or life.
And the dividing line isn’t what you say—it’s what you surrender.
Because grace is free, but it is never cheap.
It cost Him everything.

The cross wasn’t symbolic. It was brutal.
The blood wasn’t poetic. It was real.
The sacrifice wasn’t optional. It was necessary.
For you.
And now the question isn’t whether Jesus fits into your life…
It’s whether your life has been laid down for Him.

You can keep following your version of Jesus.
The one who never disrupts you.
The one who never demands change.
But that path doesn’t lead where you think it does.
Or…
You can face the real Jesus.

The One who sees everything—and still offers grace.
The One who calls out sin—but also paid for it.
The One who doesn’t just comfort you—but transforms you.

2 Corinthians 5:17 says,
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.”
Not improved.
New.
So be honest…
Is your “faith” changing you… or just accommodating you?
Because one leads to life.
And the other… quietly leads you away from Him while convincing you you’re still close.
That tension matters.

Say it plainly—no filters, no performance.
Admit where you’ve been shaping Jesus instead of following Him.
And don’t keep this to yourself. Someone close to you is doing the same thing, and no one has told them the truth.
Because halfway faith won’t hold when life breaks.
And deep down…
You already know that.
